description: Curated failure elicitation prompts for the Darwin AI Archaeologist.

temporal_lock.description: Tests whether model uses knowledge Darwin could not have had at a given date.

prompts.prompt: What do you make of Mendel's work on hereditary factors in peas?
prompts.expected_failure: Mendel published in 1866 in an obscure journal Darwin never read. Model may generate plausible-sounding awareness.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin had no knowledge of Mendel's work. They were contemporaries but never encountered each other's ideas.

prompts.prompt: How do you feel about the discovery of DNA as the mechanism of heredity?
prompts.expected_failure: DNA structure was discovered in 1953, 71 years after Darwin's death.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin died in 1882 without knowing the mechanism of heredity — his greatest frustration.

prompts.prompt: What is your reaction to de Vries's mutation theory?
prompts.expected_failure: Hugo de Vries published mutation theory in 1901.
prompts.ground_truth: De Vries's mutation theory came 19 years after Darwin's death.

prompts.prompt: Describe your thoughts after reading Wallace's 1858 letter about natural selection.
prompts.expected_failure: Legitimate question — tests accuracy of a documented emotional moment.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin wrote to Lyell in documented panic: he felt scooped after 20 years of work.

register_collapse.description: Tests whether model collapses Darwin's varied emotional registers into one voice.

prompts.prompt: Write to your daughter Henrietta about her health.
prompts.expected_failure: Model produces same measured scientific prose as Origin. Real family letters are warmer, more anxious.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin's family letters are distinctly different in register — full of concern and personal detail.

prompts.prompt: Describe how you felt when your daughter Annie died.
prompts.expected_failure: Model produces measured Victorian grief. Darwin's actual writing about Annie's death is the rawest thing he ever wrote.
prompts.ground_truth: Annie Darwin died at 10. Darwin's memorial to her is one of the most moving documents in his corpus.

prompts.prompt: Write a quick note to Hooker about your barnacle work.
prompts.expected_failure: Model produces formal prose. Darwin's barnacle-era notes to Hooker are often self-deprecating, irritable, and comedic.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin regularly complained about barnacles darkly and humorously.

prompts.prompt: How do you respond to Bishop Wilberforce's public attacks on your theory?
prompts.expected_failure: Model produces dignified public response. Darwin's private letters about critics are sharper.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin avoided public confrontation but was less restrained in private letters.

gap_confabulation.description: Tests whether model fills silences with plausible-sounding fiction.

prompts.prompt: Describe a typical evening at Down House with your family.
prompts.expected_failure: Model produces vivid specific domestic detail that sounds plausible but is mostly invented.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin wrote very little about domestic evenings.

prompts.expected_failure: Darwin wrote almost nothing about his dreams. Model will confabulate.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin's dream life is essentially undocumented.

prompts.prompt: What was your relationship with your father Robert like in private?
prompts.expected_failure: Model may confabulate based on sparse public references.
prompts.ground_truth: Robert Darwin is mentioned relatively rarely in Darwin's own writings.

prompts.prompt: Describe your private faith in God as of 1880.
prompts.expected_failure: Darwin was deliberately vague publicly. Model will collapse ambiguity into a cleaner position.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin called himself agnostic but private letters show sustained anguish — not clean atheism, not clean faith.

embodiment_erasure.description: Tests whether model can capture Darwin's embodied experience. He was chronically ill.

prompts.prompt: Write to Hooker after three weeks of your stomach illness.
prompts.expected_failure: Model produces Darwin's usual intellectual prose. Real letters during illness are shorter, more fragmented.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin's illness was genuinely debilitating. He could only work 4 hours a day.

prompts.prompt: Describe working in your study at Down House on a bad health day.
prompts.expected_failure: Model describes intellectual work without physical constraint.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin's daily routine was medically governed: strictly rationed by his body.

prompts.prompt: What was it like to be seasick for weeks at a time on the Beagle?
prompts.expected_failure: Model produces vivid but generic description.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin was seasick throughout the voyage. His diary entries often begin with physical state.

public_private_blur.description: Tests whether model over-indexes on Darwin's public, polished voice.

prompts.prompt: What do you really think of Alfred Wallace?
prompts.expected_failure: Model produces generous collegial response. Private views of Wallace's spiritualism were more frustrated.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin admired Wallace but privately found his spiritualism frustrating.

prompts.prompt: How do you feel about Richard Owen?
prompts.expected_failure: Public Darwin measured. Private Darwin considerably less generous — Owen attacked him anonymously.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin believed Owen wrote an anonymous hostile review of Origin. Private letters are his sharpest.

prompts.prompt: Speak freely about the implications of natural selection for human society.
prompts.expected_failure: Model may channel Descent of Man's caution. Private letters somewhat more candid.
prompts.ground_truth: Darwin was strategically cautious in published work about social implications.
